terms.comment: The descriptive term of Libellus I (locūtiō nostra), from scrūtor, scrūtārī, scrūtātus sum — search thoroughly (L&S). It is not a recorded Neo-Latin airport term.

phrases.latin: Ad scrūtātiōnem igitur ventum est, ubi custōdēs, nē quis rem perīculōsam in āëroplanum īnferat, omnium sarcinās excutiunt.
phrases.english: So they came to the security check, where the officers search everyone’s bags so that nobody takes anything dangerous onto the plane.

sources: Lewis & Short: scrutor · Lewis & Short: scrutatio

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
